structuralFindings: A and B use different constructs and different attainable score scales but feed the same 28% PriorityScore component.
A's theoretical qualifying maximum is 82 while B can reach 100; the 18-point setup gap can contribute 5.04 PriorityScore points.
A has an 8-point discontinuity at volumeTodayVsPrev5 0.90/0.91, equal to 2.24 PriorityScore points, even when both states pass A.
B's volume contribution is continuous from the 1.3x hard-gate threshold and can increase until 3.125x, so post-gate ranking behavior differs structurally from A.
Although code checks B before A, current A/B geometry is mathematically mutually exclusive; the precedence branch cannot decide between two simultaneously passing channels under valid definitions.
Cross-channel raw setupQuality cannot be presumed calibrated merely because both are clamped to 0-100.

falsification: If within-channel higher setupQuality has no stable outcome relation, reject the component's monotonic interpretation.

If B's apparent advantage is fully explained by genuinely better outcomes after controls, do not normalize it merely for cosmetic symmetry.

No alternative formula/weight/normalization is allowed before prospective evidence.
